summary: Root cause identified at medium-to-high confidence (top hypothesis H1, confidence 0.70 per the reviewed ranking): the cfg-3120 config change ramping pricing-engine's flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5% to 100% at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z put the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo quote path (paths=20000) on essentially all quote requests, driving pricing-engine CPU from ~40% to ~99-100% and p99 from ~60ms to ~2.5-2.9s at statistically flat traffic; order-service's 2500ms pricing-engine quote call then timed out, failing orders at the quote step. The reporter's suspicion (market-data-service dep-6111 protobuf serialization change, H2) is rejected: it landed 8 minutes before onset with a quiet interval, market-data-service shows zero errors, there is no direct order-service->market-data-service edge, and no deserialization error signature exists. Rival hypotheses (GC/resource exhaustion, redis-cache shared-dependency failure, broader blast radius) are ranked low and contradicted or untestable, though some residual uncertainty remains because no intervention/revert test was run and the config-audit shard 2/3 response was partial. The incident is still active and unresolved through 13:59Z.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Greeks v2 full-traffic flag ramp saturates pricing-engine CPU → quote timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The cfg-3120 config change ramping pricing-engine's flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5% to 100% at 12:04:00Z put the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (paths=20000) on essentially all quote requests. This drove pricing-engine CPU from ~40% to 99-100% and p99 from ~60ms to ~2.5-2.9s at constant traffic, causing order-service's 2500ms pricing-engine quote call to time out and orders to fail at the quote step.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3120 ramps flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5 -> 100 on pricing-engine at 12:04:00Z; it is the ONLY pricing-engine config change between 2026-05-01 and 12:04Z
The config-applied log lands at 12:04:16Z and the GreeksV2 path is essentially absent from the log stream pre-ramp, then saturates it post-ramp
GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo computation (paths=20000) is the slow component, taking 6465ms+ and exceeding the 2000ms quote budget
CPU steps ~40% -> 99-100% in the 12:05 bucket at statistically identical request_rate (mean ~641 vs ~641 req/s), so the step is not traffic-driven
p99 latency tracks the flagged-path share: flat ~57-63ms through the 12:04 bucket, then jumps to ~2.4-2.8s from the 12:05 bucket at a ~1.0x request_rate ratio
error_rate steps ~0.15-0.29% -> ~13% with no preceding gradual rise, matching the CPU step; failure is compute-induced not load-induced
Memory is flat (46-53%) across the transition and restarts remain 0, so the CPU step is not GC/heap pressure or a restart
pricing-engine's own errors are deadline-exceeded on the GreeksV2 calculator (2000ms budget)
order-service's only error signature is a 2500ms timeout on its pricing-engine quote call, first at 12:06:10Z, ~2 min after the pricing-engine latency jump
Orders fail at the quote step, surfacing as INC-011

assumptions: The latency/CPU step at 12:04-12:05 is caused by the flag ramp rather than a coincident unlogged event; sub-minute onset within the 12:04 bucket cannot be resolved (config-applied log 12:04:16Z, first clear degraded bucket 12:05).

The ~2.5x CPU step for a ~20x increase in flagged share is directionally consistent with the flagged Monte-Carlo path dominating CPU only when applied to most requests (F38 inference), but no per-flag request-count metric exists to measure the flagged share directly.
No pricing-engine GC metric or GC log line exists, so GC thrash is excluded only indirectly via flat memory_pct (F22/F37), not by direct GC telemetry.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Broader blast radius: multiple pricing-engine clients degraded (shared-component framing)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The fault is a shared-component failure of pricing-engine affecting all its consumers, with order-service merely the first/most visible symptom at the quote step; other pricing-engine clients would show the same degradation.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine is on the quote path (order-service -> pricing-engine -> market-data-service)
pricing-engine degrades internally (p99 ~2.6-2.9s, CPU 99%, error_rate ~12-13%)
All pricing-engine consumers experience the same latency, not just order-service

assumptions: pricing-engine has exactly ONE caller (order-service) in the service graph, so there is no second client whose telemetry could be pulled; the broader-blast-radius hop is untestable and modeled as an assumption.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / GC thrash in pricing-engine independent of any change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine reached CPU saturation (~99-100%) through resource exhaustion (GC thrash / memory pressure / thread-pool saturation) unrelated to the flag ramp or the market-data change, producing latency inflation and upstream quote timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine CPU pins at 99-100% from the 12:05 bucket onward
CPU exhaustion inflates latency and produces request deadline-exceeded errors
order-service quote calls time out at 2500ms

assumptions: No GC-pause/resolution telemetry exists (F21, F26), so GC thrash cannot be directly measured or fully excluded.
A resource-exhaustion driver would need to arise at exactly the 12:04-12:05 minute with no accompanying change, which is asserted but unevidenced.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared redis-cache dependency failure on both hops of the quote path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: redis-cache is shared by BOTH pricing-engine and market-data-service on the quote path; an eviction/cache-miss storm or redis-side degradation slowed one or both hops, driving pricing-engine latency and downstream quote timeouts independent of the serialization change and the flag ramp.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache is shared: true on both pricing-engine -> redis-cache and market-data-service -> redis-cache edges (the only shared node on the path)
A cache-side event (eviction/miss storm) reduces hit rate, increasing pricing-engine compute/latency
pricing-engine latency rises, CPU pins, order-service quote call times out

assumptions: A redis-cache event occurred with no accompanying change record; no redis telemetry was pulled (gap) so this is unverified.
A cache-miss storm would manifest specifically as the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo CPU cost observed, which is not established (F12/F18 tie the cost to the flag-gated calculator, not the cache).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporter's suspicion: market-data-service protobuf serialization change broke quote responses
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-6111 (market-data-service v5.2.0, 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf') at 11:56:00Z changed payload/format handling on the pricing-engine->market-data edge, degrading or breaking quote responses consumed via pricing-engine and causing order-service quote timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6111 switches market-data-service quote serialization to protobuf at 11:56:00Z (status live, not rolled back)
The format change degrades responses on the pricing-engine->market-data edge, slowing pricing-engine quote computation
pricing-engine p99 rises and order-service's 2500ms call times out

assumptions: That a serialization change could induce latency (rather than error) on a hop where no errors or deserialization signatures are observed.
That the change is the dominant factor despite an 8-minute quiet period with no degradation signal.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Ruled out on all four critic tests: (a) timing — dep-6111 landed 11:56Z but pricing-engine degradation begins 12:04Z (8-minute quiet gap, F16), while cfg-3120 is timestamped exactly in the onset minute (F15); (b) mechanism — the only error signature is a 2500ms timeout with zero deserialization/connection-refused errors (F7), no direct edge from order-service to market-data-service (F17), and the measured slow component is pricing-engine's internal flag-gated GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo computation (F12, F18); (c) scope — market-data-service itself shows zero ERRORs and no degradation in the window (F13).

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back pricing-engine config change cfg-3120: set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or 0) and land it now; this is the highest-confidence mitigation and targets the exact change whose timestamp coincides with the onset.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-3120 is the only pricing-engine config change since 2026-05-01 and lands in the exact bucket where pricing-engine p99 jumped 60ms->2534.9ms and CPU stepped ~40%->99%, activating the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path that is the observed slow component.

recommended_actions.action: As a secondary measure, if quote failures persist after the flag rollback, shed or throttle GreeksV2 computation (e.g. reduce Monte-Carlo paths from 20000, or disable the calculator path) before considering changes to order-service, which has no fault of its own.
recommended_actions.rationale: order-service's only error signature is a 2500ms timeout on its pricing-engine call, ~2 minutes after pricing-engine degraded; order-service itself is a symptom, not the origin.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery by confirming pricing-engine p99 returns to ~60ms, CPU returns to ~40%, and error_rate returns to <1% within two 1-minute buckets after the rollback, and that order-service quote timeouts stop.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pre-ramp baseline was p99 ~57-61ms and CPU ~38-42% at flat request_rate; a matching post-rollback profile would serve as the missing intervention positive-control test for the causal chain.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-flag / per-calculator request-count and cost telemetry (flagged-share and GreeksV2 time budget) so the flagged-path share can be measured directly rather than inferred, and add GC/heap/thread-pool metrics for pricing-engine.
recommended_actions.rationale: pricing-engine exposes only cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate and restarts; the 5%-vs-100% flagged split and any GC/thrash mechanism can currently only be inferred, and GC/thread-pool absence blocked direct exclusion of H4/H3-style alternatives.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce a staged canary with automatic guardrails for experiments that ramp expensive compute paths: ramp in small steps (e.g. 5->25->50->100) with automatic halt/rollback if p99 or CPU crosses a threshold, instead of a single-step full-traffic ramp.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-3120 moved the flag 5 -> 100 in a single step at 12:04Z, directly preceding a ~42x p99 jump and CPU pin; a guarded staged rollout would have capped blast radius and auto-reverted.

recommended_actions.action: Repair the config-audit query path (shard 2/3 returned partial in tc-006) so future incident change timelines are complete, and re-run the window-wide config/deploy query after the fix to confirm no unseen change is relevant.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partial config-audit response leaves open the possibility of an unseen config change on order-service, market-data-service or a shared dependency that could bear on the conclusion.

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back dep-6111 (market-data-service v5.2.0) as a mitigation; it landed 8 minutes before onset with no degradation signal and market-data-service shows zero errors.
recommended_actions.rationale: The market-data-service serialization hypothesis (H2) is rejected on timing (8-minute quiet gap), error signature (no deserialization errors), path topology (no direct order-service->market-data-service edge) and zero market-data-service errors.

recommended_actions.action: While validating recovery, keep the redis-cache (shared by both quote-path hops) and exchange-gateway/exchange-api dependencies under observation, and pull their telemetry if the flag rollback does not restore p99.
recommended_actions.rationale: redis-cache is the only shared:true node on the quote path, and no redis-side telemetry was pulled; it is an unexcluded alternative (H3) should the primary mitigation fail.

Evidence of a pricing-engine CPU/latency contributor that is independent of the flag: e.g. GC pause/frequency telemetry showing heavy GC thrash, a heap pressure spike, or thread-pool queue saturation coincident with the 12:04-12:05 onset, would elevate H4.

Discovery — after the config-audit shard 2/3 gap is closed — of a missed config or deployment change landing at ~12:04-12:06Z on pricing-engine or a shared dependency (e.g. redis-cache) that better explains the onset.
Telemetry showing redis-cache degradation or a cache-miss storm at ~12:04Z on either quote-path hop, which would support H3.

Evidence that the slow Monte-Carlo path was already running at ~100% of requests before 12:04Z (e.g. per-flag request counts), which would decouple the flag ramp from the CPU/latency step and break H1's mechanism.
Confirmation that other pricing-engine clients (if any exist outside the modeled graph) show the same degradation, which would support a shared-component framing over the flag-ramp explanation.

findings.statement: Across all services, the only deployment in 2026-05-20T10:00Z-13:59Z window is dep-6111: market-data-service v5.2.0, 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf' by v.rao, deployed_at 2026-05-20T11:56:00Z, status 'live', rolled_back_at null — ~20 min before the 12:16Z report.

Config change cfg-3120 on pricing-engine: key 'flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct' changed 5 -> 100 by pm-experiments at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z (full-traffic ramp). No config change in the window touches market-data-service or order-service.

Config change cfg-3118 on api-gateway: 'ratelimit.burst' 200 -> 250 by config-bot at 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z. api-gateway sits upstream of order-service (edge api-gateway -> order-service), so this is on the request path but 1h46m before the report.

order-service's quote path is a 2-hop service chain with no direct edge to market-data-service: edges include order-service -> pricing-engine (kind http) and pricing-engine -> market-data-service (kind http); order-service also calls ledger-db (db), exchange-gateway (http) and kafka (queue-produce).

redis-cache is a 'shared': true component appearing on multiple critical paths: pricing-engine -> redis-cache (cache) AND market-data-service -> redis-cache (cache), so both hops of the order-service quote path depend on the same cache; ledger-db (shared, postgres), kafka (shared) and exchange-api (external, has_telemetry false) are the other shared/external nodes in the graph.

Closest historical precedents (leads only, not evidence): HIST-113 'pricing-engine CPU saturation at market open' with symptoms 'quote timeouts','cpu 99%' (category capacity_saturation, 2026-01-28) and HIST-116 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade' (category bad_deployment, 2025-12-18) — matching the current 'quote timeouts' symptom and a change-induced failure; HIST-107 links redis-cache + market-data-service to 'cache miss storm / quote latency'.

order-service quote-timeout errors (225 total) all share a single signature — 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' — with the earliest at 2026-05-20T12:06:10Z and continuing to 13:58:24Z. There are no connection-refused or deserialization signatures in the error set.
